title: Air Pollution

sampleAnswer.full:
The image shows the process of acid rain formation, starting from industrial emissions and ending in precipitation.
First, emissions from industry, transportation, ore smelting, and power generation release nitrogen oxides and sulfur dioxide into the air. Then, these chemicals undergo a transformation into nitric acid and sulfuric acid. After that, the acids mix with clouds through condensation. Next, they fall to the ground as acid rain, fog, snow, and mist. Some gases and particles also settle as dry fallout. Lastly, it returns to emissions to the atmosphere.
To conclude, there are six steps in this process that connect to each other to create the acid rain process.
sampleAnswer.simple:
The image shows how acid rain happens.

To conclude, there are six steps in this process that connect to each other to create the acid rain process.

title: Maslow's Hierarchy

sampleAnswer.full:
This image shows Maslow’s Hierarchy of Needs in the form of a pyramid.
At the bottom of the pyramid, the Physiological needs level includes food, water, warmth, and rest, forming the base of human survival.
Above that, the Safety needs layer emphasizes security and safety, which are necessary once basic survival needs are met.
In the middle of the pyramid, the Belongingness and love needs tier refers to emotional relationships like friendship and intimacy.
Higher up, the Esteem needs category relates to respect, recognition, and feelings of accomplishment.
At the top of the pyramid, Self-actualization is shown as the highest need, representing the pursuit of one’s full potential and creativity.
Overall, the image organizes human needs from basic to complex and labels them as D-needs (deficiency) and B-needs (being), highlighting how people grow through levels of fulfillment.

title: Precipitation&Ground Water

sampleAnswer.full:
The image shows the detailed water cycle, which moves water through the land, lakes, rivers, and oceans.
First, water evaporates from lakes, rivers, and oceans. Second, plants also release water through transpiration. Third, the vapor travels through the air and condenses to form clouds. After that, precipitation falls as rain or snow. Lastly, water flows across the surface and underground to return to lakes and oceans.
To conclude, there are five steps in this cycle to show how water moves through the Earth and atmosphere.

title: Rock Cycle

sampleAnswer.full:
This image shows the cycle of rock formation, known as the rock cycle.
First, the cycle begins with igneous rock forming from cooled magma. Second, weathering and lithification turn igneous rock into sediment. After that, compaction transforms sediment into sedimentary rock. Then, heat and pressure change it into metamorphic rock. Lastly, metamorphic rock melts into magma, and it returns to igneous rock.
In conclusion, there are six steps in this cycle that connect to each other to create the rock cycle.
sampleAnswer.simple:
The picture shows the cycle of rock formation, including some steps such as magma, igneous rock, sediment, and metamorphic rock.
First of all, the cycle starts with magma cooling to form igneous rock. After that, it leads to sediment. Next, it proceeds to sedimentary rock. Then, it moves on to metamorphic rock. Finally, it returns to magma through melting.
To conclude, there are six steps in this cycle that connect to each other to create the rock cycle.

keyPoints: This image shows the cycle of rock formation, known as the rock cycle.

The cycle begins with igneous rock forming from cooled magma. Second, weathering and lithification turn igneous rock into sediment. After that, compaction transforms sediment into sedimentary rock. Then, heat and pressure change it into metamorphic rock. Lastly, metamorphic rock melts into magma, and it returns to igneous rock.
There are six steps in this cycle that connect to each other to create the rock cycle.

title: Mud Circulation

sampleAnswer.full:
This image shows the process of drilling mud treatment and solid control in oil drilling operations.
First, the process begins with the mud flow from the well head through the degasser and shaker to remove particles larger than 250 microns. Second, it continues with the desilter and desander unit to remove solids greater than 20 microns. After that, the fluid goes through centrifuges for finer solid separation above 5 microns. Then, the cleaned mud is directed to active tanks for further use. Lastly, the mud is mixed in the mixing pits before being pumped back into the well.
In conclusion, there are five steps in this process that connect to each other to create the drilling mud treatment system.

title: Forest Cycle

sampleAnswer.full:
The image shows the forest development cycle, also known as the silviculture cycle.
First, trees begin to grow in the cohort establishment phase. Second, the canopy closure phase occurs as tree crowns grow closer together. Third, the forest enters the stem exclusion phase where only some trees survive. After that, it reaches the mature phase with tall, full-grown trees. Lastly, the forest develops into an old-growth phase, and gaps form as trees die.
To conclude, there are six steps in this cycle that explain the natural growth and regeneration of a forest.

title: Water Cycle

sampleAnswer.full:
The image shows the water cycle, including transpiration, precipitation, infiltration, and evaporation.
First, water vapor rises from plants through transpiration. Second, water collects in clouds and falls as rain. Third, rainwater travels into rivers and lakes through infiltration. After that, some water forms waterfalls and moves through streams. Lastly, water from oceans evaporates and returns to the clouds.
To conclude, there are five steps in this cycle that connect together to create the water cycle.

title: Hydrological Cycle

sampleAnswer.full:
The image shows the water cycle, also known as the hydrological cycle.
First, water from oceans, rivers, and lakes evaporates into the air. Second, water also evaporates from plants through evapotranspiration. Third, the water vapor condenses into clouds. After that, precipitation falls as rain or snow. Then, water runs off the surface or soaks into the ground.
To conclude, there are five main steps in this cycle that keep water moving through the Earth’s system.
